adjudication_records.issue_text: `remove_member` in admin/groups_controller.rb uses group.save after group.users.delete, which may not persist the removal depending on the has_many :users association configuration.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)` and then calls `group.save`. In Rails, calling `delete` on an association (HABTM or has_many :through) executes the appropriate DELETE on the join table immediately; it does not rely on a subsequent `save` on the parent model to persist the removal. The finding claims the removal "may not persist depending on association configuration," but the diff does not show any unusual association setup that would make `association.delete` non-persistent, so this is speculative and not a verifiable defect introduced here. At most, `group.save` is redundant.

adjudication_records.issue_text: N+1 query in admin/groups_controller.rb add_members — one SELECT per username instead of a single User.where(username: [...]) lookup

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and inside the loop calls `User.find_by_username(username)`, which issues a separate SELECT per username. This is a verifiable per-item query pattern that can be replaced with a single bulk lookup (e.g., `User.where(username: usernames_array)`), so the finding correctly identifies an N+1-style performance issue in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: remove_member uses group.users.delete which materializes the entire users association into memory; should hit the join table directly (e.g., group.group_users.where(user_id:).destroy_all)

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `remove_member` does `group.users.delete(user_id)`. In Rails, `group.users` is an association proxy, and calling `delete` on it does not inherently materialize the entire association into memory; it typically issues SQL to remove the join record(s) (for HABTM/has_many :through) without loading all users. The finding’s core claim (full materialization into memory) is therefore not verifiably true from the diff, and the suggested alternative is an optimization/speculation rather than a clear defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members calls group.add(user) inside a loop then group.save, which can load the entire existing users association into memory on each add for large groups

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` does iterate over usernames and calls `group.add(user)` for each, then calls `group.save`. However, the finding claims this "can load the entire existing users association into memory on each add". Whether `group.add(user)` triggers loading the full association (and whether it does so repeatedly) depends on the implementation of `Group#add` / the association configuration, which is not shown or changed in this diff. From the diff alone, you can verify potential inefficiency (looping with one DB operation per user), but not the specific memory-loading behavior asserted. Therefore the finding is not a strictly verifiable problem in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: groups_controller.rb members action runs group.users.count on every page request, performing a full join-table scan for very large groups; user_count should be cached on the groups row instead

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff adds `total = group.users.count` on every request and returns it as `meta.total`. Discourse groups already have a `user_count` attribute (used elsewhere and added to the JS model), so this introduces an extra `COUNT(*)` query against the group membership association each page load instead of using the cached counter. Whether it is a “full scan” depends on DB/indexing, but the repeated count query is verifiably present and an avoidable performance regression for large groups.

adjudication_records.issue_text: group.js findMembers clamps offset to user_count rather than the last valid page start, causing next-past-end navigations to request offset = user_count, return empty pages, and leave the UI stuck

adjudication.rationale: This is a real defect in the diff. In `admin-group.js.es6` the `next` action computes `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`, so when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` it allows advancing to `offset == user_count` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50: offsets 0 -> 50 -> 100). In `group.js` `findMembers` then clamps with `Math.min(this.get("user_count"), ...)`, which preserves `offset == user_count`, and requests `/groups/<name>/members.json` with `offset=user_count`. The server (`GroupsController#members`) does `limit(limit).offset(offset)`, so `offset == total` returns an empty `members` array. The UI can thus land on an empty page at the end. (This is exacerbated by `totalPages` being computed as `Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1`, which creates an extra page when divisible.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: Breaking change to public `/groups/:name/members` response shape from a bare JSON array to an object without backward-compatibility

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `app/controllers/groups_controller.rb#members`, the response changed from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which produces a bare JSON array of serialized members) to `render json: { members: ..., meta: ... }`, i.e. an object with `members` and `meta`. There is no branching/flag to preserve the old array shape, so any existing client calling `/groups/:name/members(.json)` and expecting an array will break. The frontend was updated to match (JS now hits `/members.json` and reads `result.members`/`result.meta`), but backward compatibility for other consumers is not provided.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Admin group create/update API expects flattened top-level params instead of nested `group` params, silently breaking existing API consumers

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Admin::GroupsController#create` and `#update` to read parameters from the top level (`params[:name]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:alias_level]`) instead of the previously required nested `params[:group][...]` payload. Old clients sending `group[name]`, `group[visible]`, etc. will now be ignored: `create` will see a blank name (likely causing a validation error), and `update` will treat missing top-level `visible` as false (`params[:visible] == "true"`), potentially flipping visibility unintentionally. This is a concrete, backward-incompatible API behavior change introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Removal of PATCH-based incremental membership update endpoint causes routing errors for consumers using the PATCH verb

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the PATCH-specific incremental membership logic (`update_patch` handling `params[:changes]` add/delete) from `Admin::GroupsController`, so PATCH requests that previously modified membership will no longer have that effect. However, this does **not** create a routing error: Rails `resources` still routes PATCH/PUT `/admin/groups/:id` to `update`, and the `update` action still exists. The proposed finding specifically claims "routing errors" for PATCH consumers, which is not supported by the diff; the change is a behavior/API contract change, not a route break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Group create action no longer accepts `usernames` for initial membership in a single request

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove support for supplying `usernames` during group creation: `Admin::GroupsController#create` now only reads `params[:name]` and `params[:visible]` (no `params[:group][:usernames]`), and the JS model/controller changed from `createWithUsernames(this.get('usernames'))` to `create()`. However, the change is paired with new dedicated endpoints/actions (`add_members` / `remove_member`) and the UI now only shows the “Add members” control after the group has an `id`, indicating an intentional API/UI redesign rather than an accidental defect. So it’s a behavior change, but not a verifiable bug introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `totalPages` off-by-one error when `user_count` is evenly divisible by `limit` due to using `Math.floor` instead of `Math.ceil`

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` when `user_count > 0`. If `user_count` is evenly divisible by `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. This is verifiable and impacts behavior: the `next` action can set `offset` to `user_count` (e.g., 100), making `currentPage` become 3, and `findMembers()` will request `offset=100` which returns an empty member list from the server. Using `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` (with the zero guard) would avoid the off-by-one.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `findMembers` returns `undefined` instead of a promise when group name is empty, breaking callers that chain `.then()`

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers` was changed from returning `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` when `name` is empty to `return ;` (i.e., `undefined`). This is a behavioral/API regression: any caller that previously could safely do `group.findMembers().then(...)` will now throw when `name` is blank. While some updated call sites in this diff no longer chain `.then()`, the method itself no longer consistently returns a promise, so the finding’s core claim is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: totalPages computed property has off-by-one bug when user_count is exactly divisible by limit, using Math.floor + 1 instead of Math.ceil, producing an extra page and enabling navigation to empty pages

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` when `user_count > 0`. If `user_count` is exactly divisible by `limit` (e.g., 50/50 or 100/50), this returns one extra page (e.g., 2 instead of 1; 3 instead of 2). The `next` action uses `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, so it can set `offset` to exactly `user_count`, and `findMembers` will request that offset, which the server will return as an empty `members` list. This matches the proposed off-by-one/empty page navigation bug; `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` would avoid it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: findMembers returns undefined instead of a promise when name is empty, causing TypeError when callers chain .then() on the result

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Discourse.Group#findMembers` now does `return;` when `name` is empty, so it can return `undefined` instead of a promise. However, the only call sites changed/visible in this diff no longer chain `.then()` (the `afterModel(...).then(...)` usages were removed and replaced with plain `model.findMembers();`, and other calls just `return group.findMembers();` without chaining). Also, the UI only invokes member loading for existing groups (`{{#if id}}`), where `name` should be present. So the specific claimed failure (“TypeError when callers chain .then()”) is not verifiable from this diff alone and would require assuming other unseen callers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: addMembers and removeMember actions have no error handling (.catch), causing silent failures with no user feedback when server returns errors

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `addMembers` and `removeMember` actions do call model methods that perform `Discourse.ajax(...)` without attaching a `.catch` in the controller. However, the proposed finding’s specific claim—“silent failures with no user feedback when server returns errors”—is not verifiable from this diff alone because error reporting may be handled inside `Discourse.ajax` (a wrapper not shown here) or by a global AJAX/RSVP error handler. The diff does not demonstrate that errors are swallowed or that users get no feedback; it only shows the absence of local, explicit error handling in these actions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Member list reload (self.findMembers()) after add/remove has no error handling, showing stale data if reload fails

adjudication.rationale: In `discourse/models/group.js`, both `addMembers` and `removeMember` perform an AJAX request and then call `self.findMembers()` inside the success `.then(...)` without returning it and without any `.catch(...)`/error handling. If the reload request (`findMembers()` -> `Discourse.ajax(...)`) fails, that failure is neither surfaced to the caller nor handled locally, and the UI will continue showing whatever `members` were previously set (stale/inconsistent with the successful add/remove). This is directly verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No concurrent-request guard on pagination and member mutations, allowing race conditions from rapid clicks triggering overlapping requests

adjudication.rationale: Real issue: the new pagination and membership actions can fire multiple overlapping `findMembers()`/mutation AJAX requests with no in-flight guard or response ordering. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `next`/`previous` immediately update `group.offset` and call `group.findMembers()`. In `discourse/models/group.js`, `findMembers()` performs an async `Discourse.ajax(...)` and then `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset: result.meta.offset, members: ... })`. If a user clicks rapidly (e.g., Next twice), the first request may resolve after the second and overwrite `members` and `offset` with stale `result.meta.offset`, causing the UI to show the wrong page. Similar overlap can occur with `addMembers`/`removeMember`, which trigger `findMembers()` after mutations without coordinating concurrent requests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: add_members and remove_member controller actions silently skip non-existent usernames with no feedback to the client

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the loop does `if user = User.find_by_username(username) ; group.add(user) ; end`, so unknown usernames are indeed ignored and the action can still return `success_json` with no per-username feedback. However, this behavior existed previously and was explicitly treated as acceptable (the removed spec suite even had a test asserting it “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users”), so it’s not a clear defect introduced by this diff. Additionally, `remove_member` does not accept usernames at all (it requires `user_id` and calls `group.users.delete(user_id)`), so the finding’s claim about skipping “non-existent usernames” in `remove_member` is not accurate/verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing tests for groups_controller#members action after response format changed from bare array to { members: [...], meta: { total, limit, offset } }; pagination logic (limit/offset defaults, total count, ordering change) is completely untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `GroupsController#members` from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (bare array) to a new JSON envelope `{ members: ..., meta: { total, limit, offset } }`, and also changes pagination/ordering behavior (default `limit` 50, `offset` parsing, `total = group.users.count`, `order(:username_lower)`). In the diff, the only controller specs touched are `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb` (Admin controller), and there are no added/updated specs for `GroupsController#members` to assert the new response shape or meta/pagination semantics. So the change is effectively untested in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test verifying that add_members silently skips non-existent usernames (User.find_by_username returns nil), leaving no guard against regressions if changed to find_by_username!

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Admin::GroupsController#add_members` iterates `usernames.split(",")` and calls `User.find_by_username(username)` with a nil-check, so non-existent usernames are intentionally skipped. The previous spec coverage for this behavior existed (e.g. “succeeds silently when adding non-existent users” in the removed incremental PATCH update tests), but the new `context ".add_members"` only tests automatic-group rejection and adding real users; it does not test the non-existent-username case. So the finding correctly identifies a test coverage regression for a behavior present in the new code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test verifying that update action for non-automatic groups can successfully update alias_level, visible, and name; also missing test confirming the new flat params structure works after change from nested params[:group]

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `Admin::GroupsController#update` to accept flat params (`params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, `params[:name]`) instead of `params[:group]`, and the updated spec only adds a test for automatic groups ignoring name changes. However, the proposed finding is about *missing tests/coverage*, not a verifiable functional defect introduced by the diff. Nothing in the diff demonstrates that non-automatic updates fail or that the flat params structure is broken; it’s simply untested. Missing tests alone is not a concrete bug/security/correctness issue in the changed code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Missing test verifying that add_members and remove_member produce an appropriate error (e.g., 400) when required parameters (group_id, user_id, usernames) are missing, despite the behavioral change from params[:id] without require to params.require

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `add_members`/`remove_member` to use `params.require(...)`, which will naturally raise `ActionController::ParameterMissing` (typically a 400) if `group_id`, `usernames`, or `user_id` are absent. The proposed finding is about lacking explicit tests for that error behavior, but the absence of such a test is not a verifiable defect introduced by the diff—it’s a test-coverage suggestion rather than a real correctness/security bug in the implementation shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No integration/JS tests verifying that members list populates after asynchronous findMembers call in setupController resolves, or that pagination (next/previous) correctly updates model state, after the change from awaiting findMembers in afterModel to non-awaited call in setupController
`findMembers` returns `undefined` on empty name instead of a resolved promise, breaking promise chains for callers like `setupController` and route actions that expect a `.then` method.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `findMembers` to `return;` when the group name is empty (so it returns `undefined` instead of a resolved promise). However, within this diff all updated call sites (`AdminGroupRoute.setupController`, `group-members` route `setupController`, and the `next/previous` actions) merely call `model.findMembers()` without chaining `.then(...)`. The prior `.then`-based callers (`afterModel`) were removed in this same diff. So the specific claim that this breaks promise chains for callers like `setupController`/route actions is not verifiable from the diff (it would require other, not-shown code calling `.then`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Ajax calls in `findMembers`, `removeMember`, and `addMembers` lack a `.catch` handler, silently swallowing errors and leaving the UI in an inconsistent state on failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add `Discourse.ajax(...).then(...)` chains in `findMembers`, `removeMember`, and `addMembers` without explicit `.catch`, but that alone is not a verifiable defect in this change: missing `.catch` does not “silently swallow” errors—promise rejections will still propagate (or be handled by higher-level/global AJAX error handling, which is common in Discourse). The claim that the UI will be left inconsistent on failure is speculative from the diff alone (no evidence that errors are suppressed rather than surfaced elsewhere).

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `offset` calculation in `findMembers` clamps against a possibly stale `user_count` before the request is made, creating dead logic that can mask the intended offset and reset pagination to 0.
The `next` action in `admin-group.js.es6` caps the offset at `user_count` rather than the last-page-start, causing it to skip past the final page's start and couple incorrectly to server behavior.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin-group.js.es6` the `next` action computes `offset = Math.min(group.get("offset") + group.get("limit"), group.get("user_count"))`. That allows `offset` to become exactly `user_count`. In `Discourse.Group.findMembers`, that `offset` is sent to `/groups/:name/members.json` and the server does `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. An offset equal to the total count returns an empty `members` array, i.e. you can navigate to a blank page instead of the last page. This is especially reachable because `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which overcounts when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100/50 => 3 pages), so `showingLast` can be false on the real last page and `next` can advance to `offset == user_count`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `totalPages` in `admin-group.js.es6` uses `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, enabling paging into empty results.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit` (e.g., 100 users, limit 50), this yields 3 pages instead of 2. The `next` action allows `offset` to become exactly `user_count` (`Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`), and `findMembers` then requests `offset=user_count`, which the server (`GroupsController#members`) will return as an empty result set (`.limit(limit).offset(offset)`). This matches the finding: it enables paging into an empty page.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `group.users.delete(user_id)` followed by `group.save` is unnecessary and can cause inconsistent state if `save` fails after the membership removal already succeeded; `add_members` similarly lacks transaction wrapping.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`, the code does `group.users.delete(user_id)` (which immediately deletes the join record in the DB) and then gates the HTTP response on `if group.save`. Since no attributes on `group` were changed, `group.save` is unnecessary for persisting the membership removal. Worse, if `group.save` fails (validations/callbacks/DB error), the controller will return an error even though the membership deletion already happened, creating a response/state inconsistency. `add_members` has the same pattern: it performs membership additions inside a loop and then checks `group.save` afterward; without a transaction, you can end up with partial membership changes even if the final `save` branch reports failure.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `add_members` silently ignores non-existent usernames, providing no error path or feedback when a typo occurs in the comma-separated string.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code does `usernames.split(",").each` and only calls `group.add(user)` when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user. If a username is misspelled/non-existent, it is simply skipped with no error collection. After the loop it calls `group.save` and will return `success_json` even if zero users were added (e.g., all usernames invalid), so there is no error path or feedback for typos in the comma-separated string.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Route inconsistency: `findMembers` hits `/groups/<name>/members.json` while `removeMember`/`addMembers` hit `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`, which may not resolve correctly for PUT/DELETE depending on routing defaults.

adjudication.rationale:
The diff explicitly adds admin member routes inside `resources :groups`:
- `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`
- `put "members" => "groups#add_members"`
In Rails, routes declared directly inside a `resources` block (not inside `collection`) are **member routes**, generating `/admin/groups/:group_id/members(.:format)`. This matches the controller actions expecting `params.require(:group_id)` and the JS calls `/admin/groups/<id>/members.json`.

Separately, `findMembers` intentionally calls the non-admin endpoint `/groups/<name>/members.json` served by `GroupsController#members` for reading members. Using different endpoints for read vs admin mutation is consistent with the diff and not a verifiable routing bug introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `admin_group_route.js` calls `model.findMembers()` fire-and-forget in `setupController` instead of awaiting the promise, causing the template to briefly render empty/zero members until the async resolves.
matched_golden_ids: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same underlying problem: `findMembers()` is asynchronous but is invoked without awaiting/handling the returned promise in `setupController`, so member data may be unavailable when the controller/template renders (race/brief empty state).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `group-members.js.es6` sets `controller.model` to the group and the template iterates `members`, but `findMembers` sets `members` on the model (group), not the controller, potentially rendering nothing if the controller doesn't proxy to the model.

`usernames` in `admin-group.js.es6` is declared but never populated for display, breaking any code path that expects it to reflect current members and leaving the add-member input uncleared after additions.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, the old computed `usernames` property derived from `members` was removed and `usernames: null` is now just the backing value for the add-members `user-selector` input. The new UI displays current members via `{{each member in members}}` (populated by `model.findMembers()` setting `members` on the Group model), and saving/creating a group no longer uses usernames (`group.save()` / `group.create()` replace `saveWithUsernames` / `createWithUsernames`). So there is no verifiable broken code path that still expects `usernames` to reflect current members. It is true the input isn’t cleared after adding members (explicit `// TODO: should clear the input`), but that’s a UX improvement note rather than a demonstrated functional break in the diff, and the proposed finding’s primary claim is incorrect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `remove_member` and `add_members` use `params.require(:group_id)` but the route param is `:id`, which will raise `ParameterMissing` and cause endpoints to always return a 400 error.
matched_golden_ids: The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same root bug: the route supplies the group identifier as params[:id], but the controller actions expect/read params[:group_id] (via require), causing ParameterMissing/failed lookups and breaking the group membership endpoints.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `group.users.count` in `groups_controller.rb` triggers a separate COUNT query on every members request, coupling the public endpoint to an unindexed count with no caching.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff does introduce an additional query: `total = group.users.count` will execute a separate `COUNT(*)` before the paginated `members = group.users.order(...).limit(...).offset(...)` query. However, the finding’s key assertion that this is an “unindexed count with no caching” is not verifiable from the diff (indexes/caching behavior aren’t shown), and doing a COUNT to return `meta.total` for pagination is a normal/intentional pattern rather than a clear defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `params.require(:group_id)` in `add_members` and `remove_member` will fail in production because member routes provide `params[:id]` instead of `params[:group_id]`; tests hide this by bypassing routing and injecting `group_id` directly.
`totalPages` calculation in `admin-group.js.es6` has an off-by-one error causing an empty trailing page when `user_count` is evenly divisible by `limit`.

adjudication.rationale: In `admin-group.js.es6`, `totalPages` is computed as `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` (when `user_count != 0`). If `user_count` is evenly divisible by `limit` (e.g., 50 users, limit 50), this returns 2 pages instead of 1, creating a trailing empty page. This is consistent with the paging actions: `next` can set `offset` to `user_count`, and `currentPage` then becomes `floor(user_count/limit)+1`, which would correspond to that extra page and can yield an empty member list.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Concurrent XHRs from pagination and add/remove actions can resolve out of order and clobber state due to missing request sequencing or cancellation.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In the new code, multiple actions trigger asynchronous `group.findMembers()` calls that all mutate the same model state via `setProperties({ user_count, limit, offset, members })`. For example, `next`/`previous` set `offset` then call `findMembers()`, while `addMembers`/`removeMember` also call `findMembers()` after their PUT/DELETE succeeds. There is no request sequencing (e.g., monotonically increasing request id) or cancellation/abort of prior XHRs, so if a pagination request is in flight and an add/remove (or another pagination click) triggers another `findMembers()`, the earlier request can resolve later and overwrite `members/offset/user_count` with stale data. This out-of-order clobber is a real correctness risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `add_members` controller action silently succeeds and returns `success_json` even when none of the provided usernames exist, misleading the user.

adjudication.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, usernames are split and each is looked up via `User.find_by_username(username)`. Non-existent usernames are simply skipped (no else/raise). After the loop it calls `group.save` and renders `success_json` if the save succeeds. If none of the provided usernames exist, no members are added but `group.save` will still typically succeed, so the action returns success despite performing no changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Members panel for a newly-created group renders empty because `findMembers()` is never called after the group `id` is set during the save action.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, group creation no longer supports creating with initial usernames (`createWithUsernames` was removed). `Discourse.Group#create` sends only `{name, alias_level, visible}` and the Rails `Admin::GroupsController#create` also only sets name/visible—so a newly created group will legitimately have zero members. The members UI is gated by `{{#if id}}`, so it will appear after `id` is set, but showing an empty list at that moment is expected because no members exist yet. When members are added via the new `addMembers` action, `Discourse.Group#addMembers` explicitly calls `self.findMembers()` after the PUT, so the list will refresh then. Therefore, “renders empty because `findMembers()` is never called after id is set” is not a verifiable defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `findMembers` in `group.js` returns `undefined` instead of `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])` on empty name, which will cause errors for callers expecting a thenable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `findMembers` to `return;` when the group name is empty (previously `Ember.RSVP.resolve([])`), so it can return `undefined`. However, in the updated code shown in this diff, all call sites were changed to *not* chain `.then(...)` (e.g., routes now just call `model.findMembers();` and actions return it but don’t chain). Since there is no caller in the diff that expects a thenable, the claim that this "will cause errors" is not directly verifiable from the provided changes and relies on assumptions about external callers.
